chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih Al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The one upon whom we inflict a legal penalty (Hadd) from the penalties of Allah and he dies, so there is no wergild (Diya) for him upon us; and the one upon whom we inflict a legal penalty regarding something from the rights of the people and he dies, so his wergild is upon us.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in financial liability for the Imam when a person dies during divine versus human legal penalties?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between divine rights (Huquq Allah) and human rights (Huquq al-Nas) in the context of judicial execution, establishing that the Imamate bears financial liability for the latter but not the former. This principle reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the ruler acts as a trustee for human claims, ensuring compensation if death occurs during the enforcement of penalties like flogging or imprisonment, whereas divine penalties carry no such pecuniary burden.
